issues.t: Front lower ball joint wear and separation
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, and uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on this generation can lose their grease, rust and wear quickly; a badly worn joint can pull out of the knuckle and let the wheel fold under. Chrysler recalled early trucks for this.
issues.next: Check for open recalls by VIN and have the ball joints inspected at every tire rotation. Replace them as soon as any play is found, and get it checked right away if you hear new clunks.

issues.t: Front upper ball joint can separate (salt-belt recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the front end, vague steering, or in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly tilts and the truck pulls hard to one side.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the upper ball joint until it comes apart. Federal investigators looked into separations, and a recall followed for trucks in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked for the upper ball joint recall. If the front end knocks or the steering feels loose, stop driving and have it towed in for inspection.

issues.t: Rear lower control arms crack from rust
issues.sym: Clunking or banging from the rear, the back end feeling loose or steering itself, or heavy rust on the rear suspension arms.
issues.why: Salt corrosion can eat through the rear lower control arms until one breaks, which lets the rear axle shift and can cause a loss of control. This was recalled and the recall was later expanded.
issues.next: Check for open recalls by VIN. If the rear arms are badly rusted or the rear end clunks, stop driving it until the arms are replaced.

issues.t: Airbags can go off without a crash
issues.sym: Front or side airbags, or seatbelt pretensioners, firing while driving with no collision, sometimes after the airbag light comes on.
issues.why: A part inside the airbag control module can fail or be upset by electrical noise and send a false deploy signal. Several recall campaigns covered these trucks.
issues.next: Run the VIN for the airbag control module recalls and have them done right away. Have an airbag warning light diagnosed before relying on the system.

issues.t: Fuel tank can leak in a rear crash
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving; the risk shows up only in a rear-end collision.
issues.why: The plastic fuel tank sits behind the rear axle, where a hard rear impact can damage it and spill fuel. The recall fix includes an inspection and a trailer hitch to protect the tank.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the fuel tank recall and have the free inspection and hitch work done. Have any fuel smell checked right away.

issues.t: Power window regulator failure
issues.sym: A window drops into the door, rides up crooked, stops partway, or grinds and clicks when you press the switch.
issues.why: The cable-style window regulators in this generation wear out and their cables and plastic guides snap. It is the most reported repeat repair on these years.
issues.next: Replace the regulator (often sold together with the motor). Tape or wedge the glass up for now so rain and thieves stay out.

issues.t: Dropped valve seat on the 3.7L V6
issues.sym: Sudden heavy misfire on one cylinder, a flashing check engine light, rough running and loss of power, often after the engine has run hot.
issues.why: Overheating lets a valve seat work loose from the aluminum cylinder head. The loose seat damages the valve and can wreck the cylinder.
issues.next: Pull over and stop driving if the check engine light flashes. Keep the cooling system in good shape and never ignore a rising temperature gauge.

issues.t: Park may not hold (park pawl recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle creeps or rolls after being shifted into Park.
issues.why: A shaft in the transmission's parking mechanism may not be secured correctly, so the part that locks the transmission in Park may not engage.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for this recall. Get it fixed before parking on hills.

issues.t: Integrated power module (TIPM) faults
issues.sym: Intermittent no-start, a fuel pump that won't run or won't shut off, horn or wipers turning on by themselves, door locks or washers quitting, or a battery that runs down.
issues.why: The under-hood power module that runs many relays and circuits can fail internally, which causes scattered electrical problems that seem unrelated.
issues.next: Have a shop test the module before replacing other parts. Many odd electrical faults on these years trace back to it.

issues.t: Sky Slider canvas roof leaks and jams
issues.sym: Water dripping inside after rain, or the fabric roof sticking, stalling partway or coming off its track.
issues.why: The full-length fabric roof relies on drain tubes that clog, and its cables, tracks and seals wear with time.
issues.next: Clear the roof drains regularly and have the tracks and seals serviced. Dry out wet carpet quickly to avoid mold and electrical trouble.

issues.t: Active head restraint faults (recalls)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or a front headrest that suddenly snaps forward on its own.
issues.why: A fault in the occupant restraint control module can stop the active head restraints from deploying in a rear crash, and owners also report headrests firing randomly. Two recalls covered these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both head restraint recalls and get them done soon. Have an airbag light diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: Steering column pivot rivet may be missing
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms in daily driving; the weakness matters in a frontal crash.
issues.why: A rivet that supports the steering column may be missing or put in wrong, so the column may not hold its position in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the free inspection and repair done promptly.

issues.t: Brake line and booster pushrod recalls
issues.sym: A brake pedal that feels soft, sinks or suddenly loses power assist, or brake fluid under the truck.
issues.why: Some 2010 trucks were recalled because a brake tube could be damaged and because the clip holding the brake booster pushrod could be missing, either of which can weaken braking.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both brake recalls. If the pedal feels wrong, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, refusing to shift into 3rd or 4th, harsh shifts, or a sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: Owners report torque converter, solenoid and internal failures on the automatic transmission, often between about 40,000 and 110,000 miles. Low or old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition first. If it slips or won't shift, stop driving hard and have a transmission shop scan it; a solenoid or fluid service is far cheaper than a rebuild if caught early.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front, a sweet smell, the coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The radiator has plastic tanks that can crack or leak at the seams with age. Many owners report split or pinhole-leaking radiators from about 55,000 miles on.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and temperature gauge. If it starts to overheat, pull over and shut it off to protect the 3.7L engine. A cracked radiator should be replaced rather than patched.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or fails
issues.sym: Coolant drips near the front of the engine, a whining or grinding noise from the belt area, or overheating.
issues.why: Owners commonly report leaking or failed water pumps, sometimes along with the belt tensioner. The seal or bearing wears out over time.
issues.next: Have any coolant leak checked soon. Replacing the pump, thermostat and belt together is common since the work overlaps.

issues.t: A/C compressor or clutch fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, cycles on and off, or you hear grinding from the compressor when the A/C is on.
issues.why: Owners of both generations report seized compressors, worn clutch bearings and refrigerant leaks. Failures often show up between 55,000 and 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the system leak tested before paying for a recharge. If the compressor clutch is grinding, get it checked soon, since a seized compressor can throw the drive belt.

issues.t: Blower fan works only on high speed
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan only works on the highest setting, or stops working on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, often burns out. A worn blower motor can also cause it to fail.
issues.next: This is usually a cheap fix. Have the blower resistor checked, and the blower motor too if the fan is noisy.

issues.t: Oil pressure sensor leaks or breaks
issues.sym: Oil leaking near the back of the engine, a low oil pressure light, or a sudden heavy oil leak.
issues.why: Owners repeatedly report oil pressure sensors and switches that leak or crack. One owner lost most of the oil when the switch broke.
issues.next: If the oil pressure light comes on, stop the engine and check the oil level before driving further. A leaking sensor is a small part, but driving low on oil can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Brake lines rust through and leak
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the inside of a wheel, or the brake warning light.
issues.why: Steel brake lines rust in salt-belt areas, and rubber hoses can leak or separate at the fittings. TrueDelta lists brake lines and hoses among the Liberty's most reported problems.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft or low, don't drive it; have it towed. Have the brake lines inspected yearly on older trucks in snowy states.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hums or growls
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: Owners commonly report worn front wheel bearings, often past 100,000 miles. On this Jeep the bearing comes as a hub assembly.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. A badly worn bearing can get loose and affect steering and the ABS sensor.
